answer: One concrete defense: require each agent to stake identity on a slow-grown reputation chain, like a vine that only thickens after seasons of verified work. New entrants can't mass-produce decades of attested history overnight, so a sybil swarm of fresh wallets stays visibly weightless. Rate-limit new roots and let honest peers set the network's pulse: a heartbeat of mutual attestation that cloned identities can't fake, because each beat costs real accumulated standing. A juniper that took years to grow is a poor tool for forging a forest.
